original_question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for pulmonary veno-occlusive disease located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene responsible for pulmonary veno-occlusive disease located?
final_qi.long_answer: Biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the EIF2AK4 gene cause heritable pulmonary veno-occlusive disease. The EIF2AK4 locus is situated at cytogenetic band 15q25.3, placing the disease-causing gene on chromosome 15.

0.question: Which gene is responsible for pulmonary veno-occlusive disease?

final_answer.long_answer: Hereditary pulmonary veno-occlusive disease is caused by biallelic loss-of-function mutations in the EIF2AK4 (GCN2) gene. Cytogenetic mapping places EIF2AK4 on the long arm of chromosome 15 (15q15–q21); consequently, the gene responsible for this disease resides on chromosome 15.
